VI.description: Is this VI EXECUTABLE\3F Reads {LV.VI} Execution\3AState and VI Linker Errors through VI Server and hands both back as text.\0A\0AWHY IT EXISTS. Nothing in the generate-or-retarget chain answers this question. Measured 2026-09-09 over a ten-VI build\3A after a pylv_apply retarget the caller was Error 1003\2C not executable - and pylv_apply answered ok\3A true\2C its verify step listed all eight expected callTargets\2C the AIXML export showed every terminal wired\2C lvai_check_aixml found nothing and lvai_validate_aixml answered errorCode 0 on the source. The only way to notice was to RUN the VI\2C and a top-level UI loop never ends on its own\2C so noticing cost 2400 s and nine bisection probes. pylv_apply already names the gap in its own gatesNotChecked list - \22ExecState was not read - do it through VI Server\3B 0 means eBad\22 - so the hint was there and the reading was not.\0A\0AExecution\3AState is an enum\3A 0 eBad\2C 1 eIdle\2C 2 eRunTopLevel\2C 3 eRunning. Only 0 means broken. A VI that is merely idle reads 1\2C which is the normal answer for anything on disk that is not running.\0A\0AREAD ONLY\2C and opened WITHOUT an application instance on purpose - the same choice lvbd_coercion_dots makes\2C so this also answers while pylv_apply has the project closed. Opening and closing a VI REFERENCE does not burn the path for a later ConvertAIXMLToVI\3B only lvai_open_file does that.

Control.description: Absolute path of the VI to interrogate\2C as a string.

FreeLabel.comment: Read only: a VI reference is opened and closed, which does not burn the path.

Node.outputs: Execution\3AState:5040.state,VI Linker Errors:5040.linker,reference out:,error out:5040.error out

FreeLabel.comment: A reference that never opened must not read as eBad; that case answers -1.

Indicator.description: Execution\3AState as a number\3A 0 eBad\2C 1 eIdle\2C 2 eRunTopLevel\2C 3 eRunning. Only 0 means the VI is broken\2C and -1 means the reference NEVER OPENED - read code and source for why. That case is split off on purpose\3A a failed Open VI Reference leaves the state property unread at 0\2C which is indistinguishable from eBad\2C and a tool whose whole job is \22broken or not\22 must not answer \22broken\22 when it means \22could not look\22. Measured by pointing this VI at a .xml by mistake\3A error 1059\2C and exec state read 0.
VI Linker Errors flattened to XML. Empty when the VI has none. Flattened rather than typed so that whatever shape LabVIEW returns survives the trip back through a string.
